doc.title: Nicki Parrott interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 2, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]

title: What the shutdown does to a musician's identity, and her depression
summary: Reinventing yourself is hard; she discusses unemployment and grants, taking on the cooking role at home, and getting depressed.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: What does it do to your identity?

That’s the biggest question of all, isn’t it? Because I’ve talked to a lot of musicians and you know it’s — the word “reinvent” is not an easy word when you’ve spent your whole life committed to learning a craft, now just reinvent yourself. So yeah it’s various ways of coping I think, depending on the financial situation too. You know it’s not easy to get unemployment. I found that out. There were several grants going around but almost as quickly as they open up they close up. There’s that many people that need help. So what does it do? It makes you focus on the — prioritize different things you know. I think at

first I resented the fact that I was the one going out shopping and cooking. And then I thought well I have a role to play here, to keep the house running. And I happen to like it and they like my food. And all the rest of it, you know, it’s tough, it’s a very personal question, not easy. I certainly got depressed about two weeks in, when everything was cancelling, even into June, July. Yes, I got really depressed. And I had to reassess. I had to, you know, I have a little bit of savings, I have a supportive group around me, I have a supportive family, I have a sister that’s a musician and we talk all the time. Yeah. It hasn’t been easy but I think that the key to it is to stay creative.
